# Get transactions from the last 8 weeks excluding current week
# First, calculate the start of the current week (Monday)
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# Calculate 8 weeks ago from the start of current week
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')

# Filter transactions for the last 8 weeks excluding current week
recent_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & 
    (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    # Check if transaction occurred on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 in DAYOFWEEK)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(date_time), (1, 7))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = recent_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weeks", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_transactions = COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions = SUM(Transactions.CALCULATE(is_weekend_int = IFF(is_weekend, 1, 0)).is_weekend_int)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.ASC())

# Get customers who signed up in the last 6 months excluding current month
# First, calculate the date range
recent_customers = Customers.WHERE(
    (DATEDIFF("months", join_date, DATETIME("now")) <= 6) & 
    (DATEDIFF("months", join_date, DATETIME("now")) >= 1)
).CALCULATE(
    signup_month = JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(join_date), LPAD(MONTH(join_date), 2, "0"))
)

# Partition by signup month to calculate PMCS and PMAT
result = recent_customers.PARTITION(name="months", by=signup_month).CALCULATE(
    month = signup_month,
    PMCS = COUNT(Customers),
    PMAT = AVG(Customers.transactions_made.amount)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

start_of_this_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_window = DATETIME(start_of_this_week, '-8 weeks')

# Filter transactions to include only stocks within the defined time window.
# Also, calculate the start date of the week for each transaction and a flag for weekend transactions.
recent_stock_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (LOWER(ticker.ticker_type) == 'stock') &
    (date_time >= start_of_window) &
    (date_time < start_of_this_week)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(date_time), ("Saturday", "Sunday"))
)

# Partition the filtered transactions by the start date of their week.
# For each week, calculate the total number of transactions and the sum of weekend transactions.
weekly_transaction_summary = recent_stock_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_groups",
    by=week_start_date
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=week_start_date,
    total_transactions=COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions=SUM(is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week_start_date.ASC())

# Filter transactions for the last 8 weeks excluding current week

    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & 
    (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),

)

# Get transactions from the last 8 weeks excluding current week
# First, calculate the start of the current week (Monday)
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# Calculate 8 weeks ago from the start of current week
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-8 weeks')

# Filter transactions for the last 8 weeks excluding current week
recent_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    # Check if transaction occurred on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 when week starts on Monday)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(date_time), (6, 7))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = recent_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weeks", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_transactions = COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions = SUM(Transactions.CALCULATE(is_weekend_int = IFF(is_weekend, 1, 0)).is_weekend_int)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.ASC())

# Get transactions from the last 8 weeks excluding current week
# First, calculate the start of the current week (Monday)
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# Calculate 8 weeks ago from the start of current week
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')

# Filter transactions for the last 8 weeks excluding current week
recent_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & 
    (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    # Check if transaction occurred on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 when week starts on Monday)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(date_time), (6, 7))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = recent_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weeks", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_transactions = COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions = SUM(Transactions.CALCULATE(is_weekend_int = IFF(is_weekend, 1, 0)).is_weekend_int)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.ASC())

# Step 1: Define the time boundaries for the last 8 weeks, excluding the current week.
# The period starts 8 weeks before the beginning of the current week and ends at the beginning of the current week.
time_boundaries = GRAPH.CALCULATE(
    start_of_current_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week'),
    start_of_period=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')
)

# Step 2: Filter transactions to include only stocks within the defined time period.
# Also, calculate the start date of the week for each transaction and determine if it occurred on a weekend.
filtered_transactions = time_boundaries.Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= start_of_period) &
    (date_time < start_of_current_week) &
    (LOWER(ticker.ticker_type) == 'stock')
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(date_time), ("Saturday", "Sunday"))
)

# Step 3: Group the filtered transactions by the start date of their week.
# For each week, count the total number of transactions and the number of weekend transactions.
# The results are ordered by the week's start date.
weekly_transaction_counts = filtered_transactions.PARTITION(name="weekly_groups", by=week_start_date).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=week_start_date,
    total_transactions=COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions=SUM(is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week_start_date.ASC())

# Step 1: Extract month and symbol from daily prices
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol = ticker.symbol,
    month = JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0")),
    year = YEAR(date),
    month_num = MONTH(date)
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate monthly statistics
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(
    name="symbol_month", 
    by=(symbol, month)
).CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    year = year,
    month_num = month_num,
    avg_close = AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high = MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low = MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Calculate MoMC using PREV to get previous month's average
result = monthly_stats.CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    avg_close = avg_close,
    max_high = max_high,
    min_low = min_low,
    prev_avg_close = PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker"),
    momc = (avg_close - PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker")) / PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker")
).ORDER_BY(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC())

# Filter transactions to include only 'sell' types from the last month.
# The date_time is checked to be greater than or equal to the timestamp of exactly one month ago.
sell_transactions_last_month = Transactions.WHERE(
    (LOWER(transaction_type) == 'sell') &
    (date_time >= DATETIME('now', '-1 month'))
)

# Group the filtered transactions by their ticker symbol.
# For each group, calculate the total sell amount and the total costs (tax + commission).
spm_calculation = sell_transactions_last_month.PARTITION(name="ticker_groups", by=(ticker.symbol)).CALCULATE(
    ticker_symbol=ticker.symbol,
    total_amount_from_sells=SUM(Transactions.amount),
    total_costs=SUM(Transactions.tax + Transactions.commission)
)

# Calculate the final SPM using the provided formula.
# IFF is used to prevent division by zero if a ticker has no sell amount.
# The result is multiplied by 100.0 to ensure floating-point division and percentage conversion.
result = spm_calculation.CALCULATE(
    ticker_symbol=ticker_symbol,
    SPM=IFF(
        total_amount_from_sells > 0,
        (total_amount_from_sells - total_costs) / total_amount_from_sells * 100.0,
        0.0
    )
)

# Get transactions from the last 8 weeks excluding current week
# First, calculate the start of the current week (Monday)
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# Calculate 8 weeks ago from the start of current week
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')

# Filter transactions for the last 8 weeks excluding current week
recent_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & 
    (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    # Check if transaction occurred on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 in DAYOFWEEK)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(date_time), (1, 7))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = recent_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weeks", 
    by=week_start

    (DATEDIFF("months", join_date, DATETIME("now")) <= 6) & 
    (DATEDIFF("months", join_date, DATETIME("now")) >= 1)
).CALCULATE(

    month = signup_month,
    PMCS = COUNT(Customers),
    PMAT = AVG(Customers.transactions_made.amount)

# Filter transactions for sells in the past month
sell_transactions_past_month = Transactions.WHERE(
    (LOWER(transaction_type) == LOWER('sell')) & 
    (DATEDIFF('days', date_time, DATETIME('now')) <= 30)
)

# Group by ticker and calculate SPM
result = sell_transactions_past_month.PARTITION(
    name='ticker_groups', 
    by=(ticker_id)
).CALCULATE(
    ticker_symbol=Transactions.ticker.symbol.SINGULAR(),
    total_amount=SUM(Transactions.amount),
    total_tax=SUM(Transactions.tax),
    total_commission=SUM(Transactions.commission)
).CALCULATE(
    ticker_symbol=ticker_symbol,
    SPM=100.0 * (total_amount - (total_tax + total_commission)) / total_amount
)

# Step 1: Pre-calculate the ticker symbol and a sortable month string (YYYY-MM) for each daily price record.
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol=ticker.symbol,
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0"))
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate the monthly aggregate values.
monthly_aggregates = price_info.PARTITION(name="monthly_groups", by=(symbol, month)).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Partition the monthly aggregates by symbol. This creates the necessary context (an ancestor named 'tickers')
# for the PREV window function to operate on a per-ticker basis.
ticker_groups = monthly_aggregates.PARTITION(name="tickers", by=(symbol))

# Step 4: Access the sub-collection of monthly data for each ticker and use PREV to find the previous month's average close.
# The `per="tickers"` argument ensures the calculation is partitioned by the ticker symbol.
stats_with_prev_close = ticker_groups.tickers.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    prev_avg_close=PREV(avg_close, by=month.ASC(), per="tickers")
)

# Step 5: Calculate the final Month-over-Month Change (MoMC) using the value from the previous step.
# We use IFF to handle the first month for each ticker, where the previous average close will be null.
result = stats_with_prev_close.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    momc=IFF(
        prev_avg_close,
        (avg_close - prev_avg_close) / prev_avg_close,
        None
    )
)

# Step 1: Extract month and symbol from daily prices
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol = ticker.symbol,
    month = JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0")),
    year = YEAR(date),
    month_num = MONTH(date)
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate monthly statistics
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(
    name="symbol_month", 
    by=(symbol, month)
).CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    year = year,
    month_num = month_num,
    avg_close = AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high = MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low = MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Calculate MoMC using PREV to get previous month's average
result = monthly_stats.CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    avg_close = avg_close,
    max_high = max_high,
    min_low = min_low,
    prev_avg_close = PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker"),
    momc = (avg_close - PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker")) / PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker")
).ORDER_BY(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC())

# Step 1: Extract symbol, year, and month from daily prices for easier grouping.
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol=ticker.symbol,
    year=YEAR(date),
    month_num=MONTH(date)
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate monthly aggregates.
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(
    name="groups", by=(symbol, year, month_num)
).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    year=year,
    month_num=month_num,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Partition the monthly stats by symbol to create a window for MoMC calculation.
ticker_groups = monthly_stats.PARTITION(name="tickers", by=symbol)

# Step 4: Within each ticker's group, calculate the MoMC using the PREV window function.
result = ticker_groups.groups.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", year, month_num),
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    prev_avg_close=PREV(avg_close, by=(year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="tickers")
).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    momc=IFF(prev_avg_close, (avg_close - prev_avg_close) / prev_avg_close, None)
)

# Define a contextless expression to filter for 'sell' transactions that occurred within the last month.
# This improves readability and allows the filter logic to be defined once.
sell_transactions_in_past_month = transactions_of.WHERE(
    (LOWER(transaction_type) == 'sell') &
    (date_time >= DATETIME('now', '-1 month'))
)

# Calculate the Selling Profit Margin (SPM) for each ticker.
result = Tickers.WHERE(
    # Ensure we only process tickers that have at least one relevant transaction.
    HAS(sell_transactions_in_past_month) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    # For each ticker, calculate the total amount from sells and the total costs (tax + commission).
    ticker_symbol=symbol,
    total_amount_val=SUM(sell_transactions_in_past_month.amount),
    total_costs=SUM(sell_transactions_in_past_month.tax) + SUM(sell_transactions_in_past_month.commission)
).CALCULATE(
    # Use the intermediate values to compute the final SPM, as per the provided formula.
    # The IFF function is used to prevent division by zero if a ticker has no sell amount.
    ticker_symbol=ticker_symbol,
    SPM=IFF(total_amount_val > 0, (total_amount_val - total_costs) / total_amount_val * 100.0, 0.0)
)

# Step 1: Extract month and symbol from daily prices
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol = ticker.symbol,
    month = JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0")),
    year = YEAR(date),
    month_num = MONTH(date)
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate monthly statistics
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(
    name="symbol_month", 
    by=(symbol, month)
).CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    year = MAX(DailyPrices.year),
    month_num = MAX(DailyPrices.month_num),
    avg_close = AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high = MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low = MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Calculate MoMC using PREV window function
result = monthly_stats.CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    avg_close = avg_close,
    max_high = max_high,
    min_low = min_low,
    prev_avg_close = PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker"),
    momc = (avg_close - PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker")) / PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), year.ASC(), month_num.ASC()), per="Broker")
).ORDER_BY(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC())

# Step 1: Prepare the daily price data by creating a formatted month string (YYYY-MM) and extracting the ticker symbol.
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0")),
    symbol=ticker.symbol
)

# Step 2: Partition the prepared data by both symbol and month to calculate the monthly aggregates for each ticker.
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(name="monthly_groups", by=(symbol, month)).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Partition the monthly statistics by symbol. This creates a context where we can operate on the time series of each ticker individually.
ticker_groups = monthly_stats.PARTITION(name="tickers", by=symbol)

# Step 4: Access the monthly data within each ticker's group and calculate the final metrics.
# The PREV window function is used to get the average closing price from the previous month for the same ticker.
result = ticker_groups.monthly_groups.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    momc=(avg_close - PREV(avg_close, by=month.ASC(), per="tickers")) / PREV(avg_close, by=month.ASC(), per="tickers")
)

)

)

# ordering them in descending order.
result = combinations.TOP_K(5, by=num_transactions.DESC())

high_value_sales = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000)

# Get all payments for these high-value sales with week information
payments_with_week_info = high_value_sales.payment.CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    # Calculate the start of the week (Monday) for each payment
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in some systems, but let's use DAYNAME)
    is_weekend=IFF(
        (DAYNAME(payment_date) == "Saturday") | (DAYNAME(payment_date) == "Sunday"),
        1,
        0
    )
)

# Filter to only include payments from the last 8 weeks (excluding current week)
# Current week starts at the most recent Monday
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')  # 8 weeks * 7 days = 56 days

filtered_payments = payments_with_week_info.WHERE(
    (week_start >= eight_weeks_ago) & (week_start < current_week_start)
)

# Group by week and calculate totals
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

[DEBUG] [Q13] Code generated by gemini:
# Step 1: Prepare the data by extracting the ticker symbol and creating a sortable month string (YYYY-MM).
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol=ticker.symbol,
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0"))
)

# Step 2: Partition by both symbol and month to calculate the monthly aggregates for each ticker.
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(name="ticker_months", by=(symbol, month)).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Partition the aggregated monthly stats by symbol. This creates groups for each ticker,
# which is necessary to correctly apply the PREV window function on a per-ticker basis.
ticker_groups = monthly_stats.PARTITION(name="symbols", by=(symbol))

# Step 4: Within each symbol's group, access the monthly stats and calculate the MoMC.
# The PREV function gets the average closing price from the previous month for the same ticker.
result = ticker_groups.monthly_stats.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    prev_avg_close=PREV(avg_close, by=month.ASC(), per="symbols")
).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    avg_close=avg_close,
    max_high=max_high,
    min_low=min_low,
    MoMC=IFF(prev_avg_close > 0, (avg_close - prev_avg_close) / prev_avg_close, None)
)

# Define the time window: the start of 8 weeks ago until the start of the current week.
# This correctly captures the last 8 full calendar weeks, excluding the current one,
# with the week starting on Monday as specified.
date_boundaries = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    period_start_date=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks'),
    period_end_date=DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
)

# Start with sales over $30,000, access their associated payments,
# and filter those payments to be within our defined time window.
high_value_sales_payments = date_boundaries.Sales.WHERE(
    sale_price > 30000
).payment.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= period_start_date) & (payment_date < period_end_date)
)

# For each relevant payment, calculate the start date of its week (for grouping)
# and create a boolean flag to identify if it occurred on a weekend.
payment_details = high_value_sales_payments.CALCULATE(
    week_of_payment=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend_payment=ISIN(DAYNAME(payment_date), ("Saturday", "Sunday"))
)

# Group the payments by the start date of their week using PARTITION.
# For each weekly group, calculate the total number of payments and the sum of weekend payments.
# Finally, sort the results by the week's start date in ascending order.
weekly_payment_summary = payment_details.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_groups", by=(week_of_payment)
).CALCULATE(
    week=week_of_payment,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment.is_weekend_payment)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

result = weekly_payment_summary

# Get sales with sale price over $30,000 and their payments
high_value_sales_payments = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    # Calculate the start of the week (Monday) for each payment
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in some systems, but let's use DAYNAME)
    day_name=DAYNAME(payment_date),
    is_weekend=IFF((day_name == "Saturday") | (day_name == "Sunday"), 1, 0)
)

# Filter to only include payments from the last 8 weeks (excluding current week)
# Current week starts at the most recent Monday
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')  # 8 weeks * 7 days = 56 days

filtered_payments = high_value_sales_payments.WHERE(
    (week_start >= eight_weeks_ago) & (week_start < current_week_start)
)

# Group by week and calculate totals
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

# Define the time window for the last 8 full weeks, excluding the current week.
# The week is configured to start on Monday.
start_of_window = DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')
end_of_window = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# 1. Start with sales over $30,000 and navigate to their associated payments.
# 2. Filter these payments to fall within the specified 8-week window.
# 3. For each payment, calculate the start of its week and a flag indicating if it's a weekend payment.
#    Assuming the week starts on Monday, DAYOFWEEK will return 6 for Saturday and 7 for Sunday.
payments_to_analyze = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_window) & (payment_date < end_of_window)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend_payment=ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(payment_date), (6, 7))
)

# 4. Group the filtered payments by the start of the week.
# 5. For each week, count the total payments and sum the weekend payment flags to get the weekend count.
# 6. Order the final results by week in ascending order.
weekly_payments_result = payments_to_analyze.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_payments", by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(PaymentsReceived),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(is_weekend_payment)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

# First, we define a reusable expression to get the latest inventory status for each car.
# We use RANKING to find the single most recent snapshot for each car by its date.
# SINGULAR is then used to treat this single result as a scalar, allowing direct access to its fields.
latest_inventory_status = Cars.inventory_snapshots.WHERE(
    RANKING(by=snapshot_date.DESC(), per="Cars") == 1
).SINGULAR()

# We start by filtering the 'Cars' collection to find vehicles that meet two criteria:
# 1. The car has at least one sale record (HAS(sale_records) == 1).
# 2. The car's most recent inventory status is 'False' (is_in_inventory == False).
sold_and_out_of_stock_cars = Cars.WHERE(
    (HAS(sale_records) == 1) & (latest_inventory_status.is_in_inventory == False)
)

# Next, we partition the filtered cars by 'make' and 'model' to group them.
# For each group, we calculate the maximum sale price from all associated sale records.
# Finally, we order the results by this calculated highest sale price in descending order.
highest_sales_by_make_model = sold_and_out_of_stock_cars.PARTITION(
    name="make_model_groups", by=(make, model)
).CALCULATE(
    make=make,
    model=model,
    highest_sale_price=MAX(Cars.sale_records.sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(highest_sale_price.DESC())

# Get sales with sale price over $30,000 and their payments
high_value_sales_payments = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    # Calculate the week start date (Monday) for each payment
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in some systems, but let's use DAYNAME)
    is_weekend=IFF(ISIN(DAYNAME(payment_date), ('Saturday', 'Sunday')), 1, 0)
)

# Filter to only include payments from the last 8 weeks (excluding current week)
# Current week start would be DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
# We want to exclude current week and include 8 weeks before it
filtered_payments = high_value_sales_payments.WHERE(
    (week_start < DATETIME('now', 'start of week')) &
    (week_start >= DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks'))
)

# Group by week and calculate totals
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

high_value_sales = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000)

# Get all payments for these high-value sales with week information
payments_with_week_info = high_value_sales.payment.CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    # Calculate the start of the week (Monday) for each payment
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in some systems, but let's use DAYNAME)
    is_weekend=IFF(
        (DAYNAME(payment_date) == "Saturday") | (DAYNAME(payment_date) == "Sunday"),
        1,
        0
    )
)

# Filter to only include payments from the last 8 weeks (excluding current week)
# Current week starts at the most recent Monday
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')  # 8 weeks * 7 days = 56 days

filtered_payments = payments_with_week_info.WHERE(
    (week_start >= eight_weeks_ago) & (week_start < current_week_start)
)

# Group by week and calculate totals
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

# First, for each car, we determine its most recent inventory status.
# We use RANKING to find the latest snapshot and SINGULAR to extract the 'is_in_inventory' value.
cars_with_latest_status = Cars.CALCULATE(
    latest_inventory_status=inventory_snapshots.WHERE(
        RANKING(by=snapshot_date.DESC(), per="Cars") == 1
    ).SINGULAR().is_in_inventory
)

# Next, we filter these cars to include only those that have been sold (have sale_records)
# and are confirmed to be out of inventory based on their latest status.
sold_and_out_of_stock_cars = cars_with_latest_status.WHERE(
    (HAS(sale_records) == 1) & (latest_inventory_status == False)
)

# We then partition the filtered cars by make and model to create groups.
car_groups_by_make_model = sold_and_out_of_stock_cars.PARTITION(
    name="make_model_groups", by=(make, model)
)

# For each make/model group, we calculate the highest sale price from all associated sales.
# The partition keys 'make' and 'model' are carried over, and we use MAX() for aggregation.
highest_sales_by_make_model = car_groups_by_make_model.CALCULATE(
    make=make,
    model=model,
    highest_sale_price=MAX(Cars.sale_records.sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(highest_sale_price.DESC())

    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in some systems, but let's use DAYNAME)
    day_name=DAYNAME(payment_date),
    is_weekend=IFF((day_name == "Saturday") | (day_name == "Sunday"), 1, 0)
)

    (week_start >= eight_weeks_ago) & (week_start < current_week_start)
)

# Group by week and calculate totals
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),

# Define the time window for the last 8 full weeks, excluding the current week.
# The week is configured to start on Monday.
start_of_window = DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')
end_of_window = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# 1. Start with sales over $30,000 and navigate to their associated payments.
# 2. Filter these payments to fall within the specified 8-week window.
# 3. For each payment, calculate the start of its week and a flag indicating if it's a weekend payment.
#    Assuming the week starts on Monday, DAYOFWEEK will return 6 for Saturday and 7 for Sunday.
payments_to_analyze = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_window) & (payment_date < end_of_window)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend_payment=ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(payment_date), (6, 7))
)

# 4. Group the filtered payments by the start of the week.
# 5. For each week, count the total payments and sum the weekend payment flags to get the weekend count.
# 6. Order the final results by week in ascending order.
weekly_payments_result = payments_to_analyze.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_payments", by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(PaymentsReceived),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(is_weekend_payment)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

monthly_sales_metrics = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    # Define the time window: the start of 6 months ago and the start of the current month.
    six_months_ago_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months'),
    current_month_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
).CALCULATE(
    # Create a scaffold of all unique months within the defined time window.
    # This assumes at least one sale occurred globally in each month of the window.
    month_scaffold=Sales.CALCULATE(
        sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
    ).WHERE(
        (sale_month >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_month < current_month_start)
    ).PARTITION(name='unique_months', by=sale_month).CALCULATE(
        month=sale_month
    ),
    # Pre-filter sales to include only those from salespersons hired in 2022-2023
    # and within the specified date range.
    target_sales=Salespersons.WHERE(
        (YEAR(hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(hire_date) <= 2023)
    ).sales_made.WHERE(
        (sale_date >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_date < current_month_start)
    )
).month_scaffold.CALCULATE(
    # For each month in the scaffold, filter the target sales to match the current month.
    sales_for_month=target_sales.WHERE(DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month') == month)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate the final metrics for each month.
    month=month,
    PMSPS=COUNT(sales_for_month),
    PMSR=DEFAULT_TO(SUM(sales_for_month.sale_price), 0.0)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# First, isolate payments related to sales with a price over $30,000.
payments_from_high_value_sales = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment

# Define the time window: the 8 weeks prior to the start of the current week.
# The week is configured to start on Monday.
start_of_current_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_period = DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')

# Filter the payments to be within this 8-week window.
# Then, for each payment, calculate the start date of its week and a flag indicating if it's a weekend.
payment_info = payments_from_high_value_sales.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_period) & (payment_date < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(payment_date), ('Saturday', 'Sunday'))
)

# Partition the filtered payments by the start date of their week.
# For each week, calculate the total number of payments and the sum of the 'is_weekend' flags to count weekend payments.
# Finally, order the results by week in ascending order.
result = payment_info.PARTITION(name="weekly_payments", by=week_start_date).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start_date,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment_info),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment_info.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

    year.ASC(), 
    month.ASC()
).CALCULATE(
    year,
    month,
    total_payments,
    mom_change=total_payments - PREV(total_payments, by=(year.ASC(), month.ASC()))

monthly_sales_metrics = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    # Define the time window: the start of 6 months ago and the start of the current month.
    six_months_ago_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months'),
    current_month_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
).CALCULATE(
    # Create a scaffold of all unique months within the defined time window.
    # This assumes at least one sale occurred globally in each month of the window.
    month_scaffold=Sales.CALCULATE(
        sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
    ).WHERE(
        (sale_month >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_month < current_month_start)
    ).PARTITION(name='unique_months', by=sale_month).CALCULATE(
        month=sale_month
    ),
    # Pre-filter sales to include only those from salespersons hired in 2022-2023
    # and within the specified date range.
    target_sales=Salespersons.WHERE(
        (YEAR(hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(hire_date) <= 2023)
    ).sales_made.WHERE(
        (sale_date >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_date < current_month_start)
    )
).month_scaffold.CALCULATE(
    # For each month in the scaffold, filter the target sales to match the current month.
    sales_for_month=target_sales.WHERE(DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month') == month)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate the final metrics for each month.
    month=month,
    PMSPS=COUNT(sales_for_month),
    PMSR=DEFAULT_TO(SUM(sales_for_month.sale_price), 0.0)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

[DEBUG] [Q44] Code generated by gemini:
# Step 1: Extract the year and month from the payment_date for each payment record.
payments_info = Dealership.PaymentsReceived.CALCULATE(
    payment_year=YEAR(payment_date),
    payment_month=MONTH(payment_date)
)

# Step 2: Group the payments by year and month to calculate the total amount for each period.
monthly_payments = payments_info.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups",
    by=(payment_year, payment_month)
).CALCULATE(
    payment_year=payment_year,
    payment_month=payment_month,
    total_payments=SUM(PaymentsReceived.payment_amount)
)

# Step 3: Calculate the month-over-month change using the PREV window function.
# The 'by' parameter in PREV ensures the calculation is performed over a chronologically sorted sequence.
# The final ORDER_BY sorts the output for clear presentation.
monthly_change_calculation = monthly_payments.CALCULATE(
    payment_year=payment_year,
    payment_month=payment_month,

# Define a contextless expression to represent sales within the last 3 months.
# This makes the main query cleaner and more readable.
sales_in_last_3_months = sales_made.WHERE(sale_date >= DATETIME('now', '-3 months'))

# The main query starts with the 'Salespersons' collection.
# It filters for salespersons who have made at least one sale in the last 3 months.
# Then, it calculates the first name, last name, the total count of these sales, and the total revenue (sum of sale_price).
# Finally, it selects the top 3 salespersons based on their total revenue in descending order.
top_sales_reps = Salespersons.WHERE(
    HAS(sales_in_last_3_months) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    first_name=first_name,
    last_name=last_name,
    total_sales=COUNT(sales_in_last_3_months),
    total_revenue=SUM(sales_in_last_3_months.sale_price)
).TOP_K(3, by=total_revenue.DESC())

    (YEAR(hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(hire_date) <= 2023)

# Get payments from the previous ISO week
# The previous week starts at the Monday before the current week's Monday
# and ends on the Sunday before the current week
previous_week_payments = PaymentsReceived.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-7 days')) &
    (payment_date < DATETIME('now', 'start of week'))
).CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    payment_method=payment_method,
    payment_amount=payment_amount,
    customer_state=sale_record.customer.state
)

# Group by date, payment_method, and state to get daily totals
result = previous_week_payments.PARTITION(
    name="daily_groups", 
    by=(payment_date, payment_method, customer_state)
).CALCULATE(
    quarter=payment_date,  # Using 'quarter' as requested, though it's actually a date
    payment_method=payment_method,
    state=customer_state,
    total_sales=SUM(PaymentsReceived.payment_amount)
).ORDER_BY(quarter.ASC(), state.ASC())

# We calculate the customer's state and the specific start date of the quarter for each sale.
sales_with_quarter_info = Sales.WHERE(YEAR(sale_date) == 2023).CALCULATE(
    # Retrieve the state from the associated customer record.
    customer_state=customer.state,
    # Determine the starting month of the quarter (1 for Q1, 4 for Q2, etc.).
    quarter_start_month=IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 3, 1, IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 6, 4, IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 9, 7, 10)))
).CALCULATE(
    # Pass the customer state to the next stage.
    customer_state=customer_state,
    # Create a formatted date string representing the first day of the quarter (e.g., '2023-01-01').
    quarter_start_date=JOIN_STRINGS('-', '2023', LPAD(quarter_start_month, 2, '0'), '01')
)

# Step 2: Group the prepared data by state and the calculated quarter start date.
# Then, for each group, sum the sale prices to get the total quarterly sales.
quarterly_sales_by_state = sales_with_quarter_info.PARTITION(
    name="state_quarter_groups",
    by=(customer_state, quarter_start_date)
).CALCULATE(
    state=customer_state,
    quarter=quarter_start_date,
    total_quarterly_sales=SUM(Sales.sale_price)

    # Define the time window: the start of 6 months ago and the start of the current month.
    six_months_ago_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months'),
    current_month_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
).CALCULATE(
    # Create a scaffold of all unique months within the defined time window.
    # This assumes at least one sale occurred globally in each month of the window.
    month_scaffold=Sales.CALCULATE(
        sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
    ).WHERE(
        (sale_month >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_month < current_month_start)
    ).PARTITION(name='unique_months', by=sale_month).CALCULATE(
        month=sale_month
    ),
    # Pre-filter sales to include only those from salespersons hired in 2022-2023
    # and within the specified date range.
    target_sales=Salespersons.WHERE(
        (YEAR(hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(hire_date) <= 2023)
    ).sales_made.WHERE(
        (sale_date >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_date < current_month_start)
    )
).month_scaffold.CALCULATE(
    # For each month in the scaffold, filter the target sales to match the current month.
    sales_for_month=target_sales.WHERE(DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month') == month)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate the final metrics for each month.
    month=month,
    PMSPS=COUNT(sales_for_month),
    PMSR=DEFAULT_TO(SUM(sales_for_month.sale_price), 0.0)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

    customer_state=customer.state,
    sale_year=YEAR(sale_date),
    # Use nested IFF to find the first month of the quarter (1, 4, 7, or 10).
    quarter_start_month=IFF(
        MONTH(sale_date) <= 3, 1,
        IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 6, 4,
            IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 9, 7, 10)
        )
    )

# Define the start and end dates for the previous week, assuming the week starts on Monday.
date_boundaries = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    start_of_previous_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-7 days'),
    end_of_previous_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-1 day')
)

# Filter payments to the previous week and gather necessary information for grouping.
# This includes the payment date, the customer's state, and the payment method.
payments_info = date_boundaries.PaymentsReceived.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_previous_week) & (payment_date <= end_of_previous_week)
).CALCULATE(
    payment_day=payment_date,
    customer_state=sale_record.customer.state,
    payment_method=payment_method
)

# Partition the filtered payments by day, state, and payment method to create distinct groups.
# Then, calculate the sum of payment amounts for each group.
daily_totals_by_group = payments_info.PARTITION(
    name="payment_groups",
    by=(payment_day, customer_state, payment_method)
).CALCULATE(
    quarter=payment_day,
    state=customer_state,
    payment_method=payment_method,
    total_sales=SUM(PaymentsReceived.payment_amount)
)

# Order the final results by date (quarter) and then by state.
result = daily_totals_by_group.ORDER_BY(quarter.ASC(), state.ASC())

# Get payments from the previous ISO week
# First, calculate the start and end of the previous week
previous_week_payments = PaymentsReceived.WHERE(
    # Previous week starts at: current date - days since Monday - 7 more days
    # Previous week ends at: current date - days since Monday - 1 day
    (payment_date >= DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-7 days')) &
    (payment_date < DATETIME('now', 'start of week'))
).CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    payment_method=payment_method,
    payment_amount=payment_amount,
    customer_state=sale_record.customer.state
)

    state=customer_state,
    total_sales=SUM(PaymentsReceived.payment_amount)
).ORDER_BY(quarter.ASC(), state.ASC())

# Step 1: Filter sales for the year 2023 and prepare the data for grouping.
# We calculate the customer's state and the specific start date of the quarter for each sale.
sales_with_quarter_info = Sales.WHERE(YEAR(sale_date) == 2023).CALCULATE(
    # Retrieve the state from the associated customer record.
    customer_state=customer.state,
    # Determine the starting month of the quarter (1 for Q1, 4 for Q2, etc.).
    quarter_start_month=IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 3, 1, IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 6, 4, IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 9, 7, 10)))
).CALCULATE(
    # Pass the customer state to the next stage.
    customer_state=customer_state,
    # Create a formatted date string representing the first day of the quarter (e.g., '2023-01-01').
    quarter_start_date=JOIN_STRINGS('-', '2023', LPAD(quarter_start_month, 2, '0'), '01')
)

# Step 2: Group the prepared data by state and the calculated quarter start date.
# Then, for each group, sum the sale prices to get the total quarterly sales.
quarterly_sales_by_state = sales_with_quarter_info.PARTITION(
    name="state_quarter_groups",
    by=(customer_state, quarter_start_date)
).CALCULATE(
    state=customer_state,
    quarter=quarter_start_date,
    total_quarterly_sales=SUM(Sales.sale_price)
)

monthly_sales_metrics = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    # Define the time window: the start of 6 months ago and the start of the current month.
    six_months_ago_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months'),
    current_month_start=DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
).CALCULATE(
    # Create a scaffold of all unique months within the defined time window.
    # This assumes at least one sale occurred globally in each month of the window.
    month_scaffold=Sales.CALCULATE(
        sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
    ).WHERE(
        (sale_month >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_month < current_month_start)
    ).PARTITION(name='unique_months', by=sale_month).CALCULATE(
        month=sale_month
    ),
    # Pre-filter sales to include only those from salespersons hired in 2022-2023
    # and within the specified date range.
    target_sales=Salespersons.WHERE(
        (YEAR(hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(hire_date) <= 2023)
    ).sales_made.WHERE(
        (sale_date >= six_months_ago_start) & (sale_date < current_month_start)
    )
).month_scaffold.CALCULATE(
    # For each month in the scaffold, filter the target sales to match the current month.
    sales_for_month=target_sales.WHERE(DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month') == month)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate the final metrics for each month.
    month=month,
    PMSPS=COUNT(sales_for_month),
    PMSR=DEFAULT_TO(SUM(sales_for_month.sale_price), 0.0)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

    # Determine the starting month of the quarter (1 for Q1, 4 for Q2, etc.).
    quarter_start_month=IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 3, 1, IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 6, 4, IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 9, 7, 10)))
).CALCULATE(
    # Pass the customer state to the next stage.
    customer_state=customer_state,
    # Create a formatted date string representing the first day of the quarter (e.g., '2023-01-01').
    quarter_start_date=JOIN_STRINGS('-', '2023', LPAD(quarter_start_month, 2, '0'), '01')
)

# Step 2: Group the prepared data by state and the calculated quarter start date.
# Then, for each group, sum the sale prices to get the total quarterly sales.
quarterly_sales_by_state = sales_with_quarter_info.PARTITION(
    name="state_quarter_groups",
    by=(customer_state, quarter_start_date)
).CALCULATE(
    state=customer_state,
    quarter=quarter_start_date,
    total_quarterly_sales=SUM(Sales.sale_price)
)

    sale_price=sale_price,
    customer_state=customer.state,
    quarter=IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 3, 1,
             IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 6, 2,
             IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 9, 3, 4))),
    quarter_start_date=IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 3, '2023-01-01',

                       IFF(MONTH(sale_date) <= 9, '2023-07-01', '2023-10-01')))
)

    state=customer_state,
    quarter_date=quarter_start_date,
    total_sales=SUM(Sales.sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(state.ASC(), quarter_date.ASC())

    first_treatment_year=YEAR(MIN(treatments_received.start_dt))
)

# Step 2: Group by the first treatment year and count the number of new patients for each year.
yearly_new_patient_counts = patient_first_treatment_info.PARTITION(
    name="yearly_groups", by=first_treatment_year
).CALCULATE(
    year=first_treatment_year,
    num_new_patients=COUNT(Patients)
)

# Step 3: Calculate the year-over-year increase (NPI) using the PREV function and order the final result.

    year=year,
    num_new_patients=num_new_patients,
    npi=num_new_patients - PREV(num_new_patients, by=year.ASC())
).ORDER_BY(year.ASC())

    start_of_window=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-12 months')
)

# Filter treatments to this window and create a 'yyyy-mm' field for grouping.
treatments_in_window = time_info.Treatments.WHERE(
    (start_dt >= start_of_window) & (start_dt < start_of_current_month)
).CALCULATE(
    treatment_month=JOIN_STRINGS('-', YEAR(start_dt), LPAD(MONTH(start_dt), 2, '0'))
)

# Partition by month and calculate the required metrics.
# PMPD: Per Month Patient Diagnoses (distinct count of patients).
# PMTC: Per Month Treatment Count (total count of treatments).
monthly_metrics = treatments_in_window.PARTITION(name="monthly_groups", by=treatment_month).CALCULATE(
    month=treatment_month,
    PMPD=NDISTINCT(Treatments.patient_id),
    PMTC=COUNT(Treatments)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

    first_treatment_year=YEAR(MIN(treatments_received.start_dt))
)

    year=year,
    num_new_patients=num_new_patients,

# First, we filter the Doctors collection to include only those who were registered two years from the current year.
# Then, for each of these doctors, we access their prescribed treatments.
# We use the RANKING window function to identify the very first treatment for each doctor by ordering their treatments by the start date in ascending order.
# The 'per="Doctors"' argument ensures that the ranking is performed separately for each doctor.
# Finally, we select the doctor's last name, their registration year, and the ID and start date of their first treatment.

    year_reg == YEAR(DATETIME('now')) - 2

).CALCULATE(
    last_name=doctor.last_name,
    year_reg=doctor.year_reg,
    first_treatment_id=treatment_id,
    first_treatment_date=start_dt
)

# Get notifications from US and Canada users for the last 3 weeks excluding current week
us_canada_notifications = Users.WHERE(
    (LOWER(country) == LOWER('US')) | (LOWER(country) == LOWER('Canada'))
).notifications.WHERE(
    # Filter for last 3 weeks excluding current week
    (DATEDIFF("weeks", created_at, DATETIME('now')) >= 1) & 
    (DATEDIFF("weeks", created_at, DATETIME('now')) <= 3)
).CALCULATE(
    # Truncate created_at to start of week
    week_start = DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    # Check if notification was sent on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(created_at), (1, 7))
)

# Partition by week and calculate totals
result = us_canada_notifications.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_groups", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_notifications = COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications = SUM(Notifications.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.DESC())

# Define the time window: the start of three weeks ago and the start of the current week.
start_of_current_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_time_window = DATETIME(start_of_current_week, '-3 weeks')

# 1. Start with notifications and add calculated columns for the week and weekend status.
#    Also, pre-filter notifications to the relevant time window for efficiency.
notification_info = Ewallet.Notifications.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_time_window) & (created_at < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    notification_week=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(created_at), ('Saturday', 'Sunday')),
    user_country=user.country
)

# 2. Filter these notifications to include only those from users in the US or Canada.
#    This approach filters notifications first, which can be more efficient than filtering all users.
country_notifications = notification_info.WHERE(
    ISIN(user_country, ('US', 'Canada'))
)

# 3. Partition the filtered notifications by week to aggregate the counts.
weekly_summary = country_notifications.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_notifications", by=notification_week
).CALCULATE(
    week=notification_week,
    total_notifications=COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications=SUM(is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

    (LOWER(country) == LOWER('US')) | (LOWER(country) == LOWER('Canada'))
).notifications.WHERE(
    # Filter for last 3 weeks excluding current week
    (DATEDIFF("weeks", created_at, DATETIME('now')) >= 1) & 
    (DATEDIFF("weeks", created_at, DATETIME('now')) <= 3)
).CALCULATE(
    # Truncate created_at to start of week
    week_start = DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    # Check if notification was sent on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(created_at), (1, 7))
)

# Partition by week and calculate totals

    name="weekly_groups", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_notifications = COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications = SUM(Notifications.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.DESC())

# Define the time window: the start of three weeks ago and the start of the current week.
start_of_current_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_time_window = DATETIME(start_of_current_week, '-3 weeks')

# 1. Start with notifications and add calculated columns for the week and weekend status.
#    Also, pre-filter notifications to the relevant time window for efficiency.
notification_info = Ewallet.Notifications.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_time_window) & (created_at < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    notification_week=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(created_at), ('Saturday', 'Sunday')),
    user_country=user.country
)

# 2. Filter these notifications to include only those from users in the US or Canada.
#    This approach filters notifications first, which can be more efficient than filtering all users.
country_notifications = notification_info.WHERE(
    ISIN(user_country, ('US', 'Canada'))
)

# 3. Partition the filtered notifications by week to aggregate the counts.
weekly_summary = country_notifications.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_notifications", by=notification_week
).CALCULATE(
    week=notification_week,
    total_notifications=COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications=SUM(is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

).notifications.WHERE(
    # Filter for last 3 weeks excluding current week
    (DATEDIFF("weeks", created_at, DATETIME('now')) >= 1) & 
    (DATEDIFF("weeks", created_at, DATETIME('now')) <= 3)
).CALCULATE(
    # Truncate created_at to start of week
    week_start = DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    # Check if it's a weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 based on start_of_week config)

)

# Define the time window: the start of the current week and the start of the 3-week lookback period.
start_of_current_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_period = DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-3 weeks')

# 1. Filter for notifications sent to users in the US or Canada.
# 2. Further filter these notifications to include only those created within the last 3 weeks, excluding the current week.
notifications_in_scope = Ewallet.Users.WHERE(
    ISIN(country, ('US', 'Canada'))
).notifications.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_period) & (created_at < start_of_current_week)
)

# 3. Prepare the filtered data for aggregation.
#    - 'notification_week' is calculated by truncating the 'created_at' timestamp to the start of its week.
#    - 'is_weekend' is a flag (1 or 0) indicating if the notification was sent on a Saturday or Sunday.
notifications_prepared = notifications_in_scope.CALCULATE(
    notification_week=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=IFF(ISIN(DAYNAME(created_at), ('Saturday', 'Sunday')), 1, 0)
)

# 4. Partition the prepared notifications by 'notification_week' to group them.
# 5. For each weekly group, calculate the total number of notifications and the sum of the 'is_weekend' flags to get the weekend count.
result = notifications_prepared.PARTITION(name="weekly_groups", by=notification_week).CALCULATE(
    week=notification_week,
    total_notifications=COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications=SUM(Notifications.is_weekend)
)

# Define the start of the current month and two months prior to establish the time window.
start_of_current_month = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
start_of_two_months_ago = DATETIME(start_of_current_month, '-2 months')

# Filter transactions for the last two full months and for sender_type 0.
# Pre-calculate date components (year, month, day) for partitioning.
transactions_in_period = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_two_months_ago) &
    (created_at < start_of_current_month) &
    (sender_type == 0)
).CALCULATE(
    tx_year=YEAR(created_at),
    tx_month=MONTH(created_at),
    tx_day=DAY(created_at),
    sender_id=sender_id
)

# First, partition by day to calculate the Daily Active Users (DAU).
# DAU is the number of distinct senders for each day.
daily_users = transactions_in_period.PARTITION(
    name="daily_groups",
    by=(tx_year, tx_month, tx_day)
).CALCULATE(
    tx_year=tx_year,
    tx_month=tx_month,
    dau=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
)

# Second, partition the daily results by month to calculate the average DAU for each month (PMDAU).
pmdau_calculation = daily_users.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups",
    by=(tx_year, tx_month)
).CALCULATE(
    month_formatted=JOIN_STRINGS('-', tx_year, LPAD(tx_month, 2, '0')),

# Step 1: Define the time boundaries for the last two full months.
time_boundaries = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    start_of_current_month=DATETIME('now', 'start of month'),
    start_of_period=DATETIME(DATETIME('now', 'start of month'), '-2 months')
)

# Step 2: Filter transactions for the specified period and sender type, and extract the day.
transactions_in_period = time_boundaries.Transactions.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_period) &
    (created_at < start_of_current_month) &
    (sender_type == 0)
).CALCULATE(
    transaction_day=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of day'),
    sender_id
)

# Step 3: Calculate Daily Active Users (DAU) by partitioning by day and counting distinct senders.
daily_active_users = transactions_in_period.PARTITION(name="days", by=transaction_day).CALCULATE(
    transaction_day=transaction_day,
    dau=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
)

# Step 4: Calculate PMDAU by partitioning the daily stats by month and averaging the DAU.
# First, create a month column in 'yyyy-mm' format.
# Then, partition by that month and calculate the average of the daily counts.
pmdau_by_month = daily_active_users.CALCULATE(
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(transaction_day), LPAD(MONTH(transaction_day), 2, "0")),
    dau=dau
).PARTITION(name="months", by=month).CALCULATE(
    month=month,
    pmdau=AVG(daily_active_users.dau)
)

result = pmdau_by_month

# Define the start of the current month and the previous month using the DATETIME function.
# 'start of month' truncates the current timestamp to the beginning of the month.
# '-1 month' subtracts one month from that date to get the start of the previous month.
start_of_current_month = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
start_of_previous_month = DATETIME(start_of_current_month, '-1 month')

# Filter the Transactions collection to include only those created within the previous month.
# The condition checks if 'created_at' is on or after the start of the previous month
# and before the start of the current month.
transactions_in_prev_month = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_previous_month) & (created_at < start_of_current_month)
)

# Calculate the Success Transaction Rate (STR) at the top Ewallet level.
# First, calculate the count of successful transactions (status is 'success', case-insensitive)
# and the total number of transactions for the filtered period.
# Then, in a subsequent CALCULATE, compute the STR by dividing the successful count by the total count.
# IFF is used to handle the case where there are no transactions, preventing division by zero and returning 0.0.
result = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    successful_transactions_count=COUNT(transactions_in_prev_month.WHERE(LOWER(status) == 'success')),
    total_transactions_count=COUNT(transactions_in_prev_month)
).CALCULATE(
    str=IFF(total_transactions_count > 0, successful_transactions_count / total_transactions_count, 0.0)
)

# and prepare fields for grouping.
tx_info = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (sender_type == 0) &
    (created_at >= DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-2 months')) &
    (created_at < DATETIME('now', 'start of month'))
).CALCULATE(
    month_str=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(created_at), LPAD(MONTH(created_at), 2, "0")),
    day_date=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of day')
)

# Step 2: Group by month and day to calculate Daily Active Users (DAU).
# This gives us the number of distinct users for each day.
daily_active_users = tx_info.PARTITION(name="daily_groups", by=(month_str, day_date)).CALCULATE(
    month_str=month_str,
    dau=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
)

# Step 3: Group the daily stats by month to calculate the average DAU, which is the PMDAU.
pmdau_result = daily_active_users.PARTITION(name="monthly_groups", by=month_str).CALCULATE(
    month=month_str,
    pmdau=AVG(daily_groups.dau)
)

# Step 1: Define the time boundaries for the last two full months.
time_boundaries = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    start_of_current_month=DATETIME('now', 'start of month'),
    start_of_period=DATETIME(DATETIME('now', 'start of month'), '-2 months')
)

# Step 2: Filter transactions for the specified period and sender type, and extract the day.
transactions_in_period = time_boundaries.Transactions.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_period) &
    (created_at < start_of_current_month) &
    (sender_type == 0)
).CALCULATE(
    transaction_day=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of day'),
    sender_id
)

# Step 3: Calculate Daily Active Users (DAU) by partitioning by day and counting distinct senders.
daily_active_users = transactions_in_period.PARTITION(name="days", by=transaction_day).CALCULATE(
    transaction_day=transaction_day,
    dau=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
)

# Step 4: Calculate PMDAU by partitioning the daily stats by month and averaging the DAU.
# First, create a month column in 'yyyy-mm' format.
# Then, partition by that month and calculate the average of the daily counts.
pmdau_by_month = daily_active_users.CALCULATE(
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(transaction_day), LPAD(MONTH(transaction_day), 2, "0")),
    dau=dau
).PARTITION(name="months", by=month).CALCULATE(
    month=month,
    pmdau=AVG(daily_active_users.dau)
)

result = pmdau_by_month

# Define the start of the current month and the previous month using the DATETIME function.
# 'start of month' truncates the current timestamp to the beginning of the month.
# '-1 month' subtracts one month from that date to get the start of the previous month.
start_of_current_month = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
start_of_previous_month = DATETIME(start_of_current_month, '-1 month')

# Filter the Transactions collection to include only those created within the previous month.
# The condition checks if 'created_at' is on or after the start of the previous month
# and before the start of the current month.
transactions_in_prev_month = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_previous_month) & (created_at < start_of_current_month)
)

# Calculate the Success Transaction Rate (STR) at the top Ewallet level.
# First, calculate the count of successful transactions (status is 'success', case-insensitive)
# and the total number of transactions for the filtered period.
# Then, in a subsequent CALCULATE, compute the STR by dividing the successful count by the total count.
# IFF is used to handle the case where there are no transactions, preventing division by zero and returning 0.0.
result = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    successful_transactions_count=COUNT(transactions_in_prev_month.WHERE(LOWER(status) == 'success')),
    total_transactions_count=COUNT(transactions_in_prev_month)
).CALCULATE(
    str=IFF(total_transactions_count > 0, successful_transactions_count / total_transactions_count, 0.0)
)

    merchant_creation_year=YEAR(created_at),
    merchant_creation_month=MONTH(created_at)
).CALCULATE(
    merchant_id=mid,
    merchant_name=name,
    num_coupons=COUNT(coupons.WHERE(
        (YEAR(created_at) == merchant_creation_year) & (MONTH(created_at) == merchant_creation_month)
    ))
)

# Then, use TOP_K to find the single merchant with the highest count of these coupons.
top_merchant_by_coupons = merchant_coupon_counts.TOP_K(1, by=num_coupons.DESC())

transactions_2023 = Transactions.WHERE(
    (YEAR(created_at) == 2023) & 
    (LOWER(status) == 'success') & 
    (sender_type == 0)
).CALCULATE(
    year_month = JOIN_STRINGS('-', YEAR(created_at), LPAD(MONTH(created_at), 2, '0')),
    sender_id = sender_id
)

# Partition by month and count distinct users

    name='months', 
    by=year_month
).CALCULATE(
    month = year_month,
    active_users = NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# First, let's get users with their country and filter for those who sent transactions with sender_type = 0
user_country_info = Users.WHERE(
    HAS(transactions_sent.WHERE(sender_type == 0)) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    user_country=country,
    user_id=uid,
    total_sent=SUM(transactions_sent.WHERE(sender_type == 0).amount)
)

# Now partition by country to aggregate the data
country_stats = user_country_info.PARTITION(
    name="countries", 
    by=user_country
).CALCULATE(
    country=user_country,
    num_distinct_users=COUNT(Users),
    total_transaction_amount=SUM(Users.total_sent)
)

# Get the top 5 countries by total transaction amount
result = country_stats.TOP_K(5, by=total_transaction_amount.DESC())

# Define the start of the current month and the start of the previous month
start_of_current_month = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
start_of_previous_month = DATETIME(start_of_current_month, '-1 month')

# Calculate the Success Transaction Rate (STR) for the previous month
previous_month_str = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    # First, filter all transactions to get only those from the previous month
    transactions_in_period=Transactions.WHERE(
        (created_at >= start_of_previous_month) & (created_at < start_of_current_month)
    )
).CALCULATE(
    # From the filtered set, count the successful and total transactions
    successful_tx_count=COUNT(transactions_in_period.WHERE(LOWER(status) == 'success')),
    total_tx_count=COUNT(transactions_in_period)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate the final STR, handling the case of zero total transactions
    str_rate=IFF(total_tx_count > 0, successful_tx_count / total_tx_count, 0.0)
)

    merchant_id=mid,

# Define a contextless expression to find the single earliest coupon for each merchant.
# This is done by ranking the coupons by their start date in ascending order for each merchant
# and selecting the top-ranked one. SINGULAR() is used to treat the result as a single record.
earliest_coupon_for_merchant = Merchants.coupons.WHERE(
    RANKING(by=start_date.ASC(), per="Merchants", allow_ties=False) == 1
).SINGULAR()

# Filter merchants to find those whose earliest coupon's start date is within 365 days
# of the merchant's creation date. It first ensures the merchant has at least one coupon.
merchants_with_early_coupons = Merchants.WHERE(HAS(coupons) == 1).WHERE(
    DATEDIFF("days", created_at, earliest_coupon_for_merchant.start_date) <= 365
)

# Select the required fields: merchant ID, registration date, and the ID and start date
# of the earliest coupon.
result = merchants_with_early_coupons.CALCULATE(
    merchant_id=mid,
    registration_date=created_at,
    earliest_coupon_id=earliest_coupon_for_merchant.cid,
    earliest_coupon_start_date=earliest_coupon_for_merchant.start_date
)

# First, we filter the MerchantBalances collection to get only the records updated today.
# We use DATETIME('now', 'start of day') to ensure we are comparing only the date part.
todays_balances = Ewallet.MerchantBalances.WHERE(
    DATETIME(updated_at, 'start of day') == DATETIME('now', 'start of day')
)

# Next, we filter these daily balances to include only those from merchants
# who are 'active' and whose category contains 'retail'.
# We access the merchant's properties through the 'merchant' relationship.
# LOWER() and CONTAINS() are used for case-insensitive and partial string matching.
filtered_merchant_balances = todays_balances.WHERE(
    (LOWER(merchant.status) == 'active') & (CONTAINS(LOWER(merchant.category), 'retail'))
)

# Finally, we calculate the median of the 'balance' from the resulting set of filtered balances.
result = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    median_balance=MEDIAN(filtered_merchant_balances.balance)
)

[DEBUG] [Q118] Code generated by gemini:
# First, filter transactions to include only those sent by users (sender_type == 0)
# and retrieve the sender's country for each transaction.
transactions_with_country_info = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(sender_type == 0).CALCULATE(
    country=sending_user.country
)

# Next, partition the filtered transactions by country to create groups for aggregation.
country_groups = transactions_with_country_info.PARTITION(name="countries", by=country)

# Then, for each country group, calculate the number of distinct users and the sum of transaction amounts.
# We access the 'Transactions' sub-collection within each partition to perform the aggregations.
country_transaction_summary = country_groups.CALCULATE(
    country=country,
    num_distinct_users=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sending_user.uid),
    total_transaction_amount=SUM(Transactions.amount)
)

# Finally, select the top 5 countries based on the total transaction amount in descending order.
top_5_countries_by_sent_amount = country_transaction_summary.TOP_K(5, by=total_transaction_amount.DESC())

# First, for each user, we define the relevant time window: the sign-up date and the date one year later.
users_with_date_range = Ewallet.Users.CALCULATE(
    signup_date=created_at,
    first_year_end_date=DATETIME(created_at, '1 year')
)

# Next, we filter these users. The HASNOT function checks for the absence of notifications 
# within the calculated one-year window. The fields 'signup_date' and 'first_year_end_date' 
# are available inside the nested WHERE clause.
users_without_first_year_notifications = users_with_date_range.WHERE(
    HASNOT(notifications.WHERE(
        (created_at >= signup_date) & (created_at < first_year_end_date)
    )) == 1
)

# Finally, we select the username, email, and the original sign-up date for the filtered users.
result = users_without_first_year_notifications.CALCULATE(
    username=username,
    email=email,
    signup_date=signup_date
)

    transaction_amount=amount
